# TenkaCloud — task guide for LLM assistants

TenkaCloud is Apache 2.0 software for local Docker drills and AWS-hosted events. Answer in the user's
language. Use their stated goal and existing context; do not ask them to choose again.
This guide is a map to current sources, not a substitute for checking the code or runtime.

## Instructions for the agent reading this

| User goal | Read first | First observable result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Try locally, no AWS | [Local hosting](https://github.com/susumutomita/TenkaCloud/blob/main/docs/local-hosting.md) | Portal opens, a supported drill starts, and the requested answer produces a result |
| Host an event on AWS | [Organizer manual](https://tenkacloud.com/docs/manual/organizer/index.en.html) | Admin and participant can sign in; a test team's answer appears in the score |
| Check cloud readiness or costs | [Cloud implementation status](https://github.com/susumutomita/TenkaCloud/blob/main/infrastructure/README.md) | Separate implemented checks, incomplete features and unverified real-AWS costs |
| Join an event | [Participant manual](https://tenkacloud.com/docs/manual/participant/index.en.html) | The team's selected problem accepts its first action |
| Change code | [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/susumutomita/TenkaCloud/blob/main/AGENTS.md) and [developer manual](https://tenkacloud.com/docs/manual/developer/index.en.html) | A focused change with relevant verification and explicit remaining limits |
| Add a problem | [Problem author manual](https://tenkacloud.com/docs/manual/problem-author/index.en.html) | Catalog/pack validation and a supported participant flow |

## Local hosting

Use the [current quickstart](https://github.com/susumutomita/TenkaCloud#quickstart).
The checkout uses its pinned Bun and Node.js tools; Docker and Compose are needed
for container problems. `make install` installs dependencies without lifecycle
scripts. `make local` starts the organizer and participant consoles and SQLite.
Open the printed URLs. `make down` stops this host's owned runtimes and preserves
event data, scores, editor drafts and resumable problem state. It does not clear
shared Docker caches or other projects.
For a remote development workspace, [Codespaces](https://codespaces.new/susumutomita/TenkaCloud)
is available; check its compute costs and forwarded-origin configuration rather
than assuming the localhost browser flow has been rehearsed there.

Local hosting prepares team/problem entries without starting every container.
Participants start, stop and resume their own problems within configured active
limits. Catalog visibility is not proof that every hardware/runtime variant was
rehearsed. AWS-service problems require cloud hosting. Follow each problem's
scoring contract rather than requiring a flag-shaped string for every answer.
The [browser demo](https://tenkacloud.com/portal-demo/?demo=1&goto=start) is a separate
preview and does not establish a shared competition's authentication or scores.

## Cloud hosting and the deployment launcher

The single console launcher is
[`infrastructure/templates/cloud-pipeline.yaml`](https://github.com/susumutomita/TenkaCloud/blob/main/infrastructure/templates/cloud-pipeline.yaml).
It preserves the previous full deployment and teardown flow and its fixed
platform/catalog refs. The filename change does not switch those refs to the
unfinished current Lambda/DynamoDB restoration. See the
[deployment guide](https://github.com/susumutomita/TenkaCloud/blob/main/DEPLOYMENT_GUIDE.md)
for that pinned flow, permissions, retained resources and destructive cleanup.
Creating the launcher alone does not deploy the platform: a deployment administrator
explicitly starts CodeBuild. Its role can execute source and command overrides,
so access belongs only to trusted deployment administrators. AWS resources and
build time can incur charges. Do not promise zero cost or invoke teardown merely
because a deployment failed. In the pinned flow, `ACTION=destroy` and
`ACTION=destroy-all` have different retained-data consequences; follow the pinned
guide instead of treating either as a simple stop command.

The current integration uses local SQLite and restores Lambda/DynamoDB for cloud
hosting without SaaS/SBT. Its `make deploy` and `make destroy` remain fail-safe
placeholders while initial IAM setup, coordinated exercise teardown and remaining
runtimes are unfinished. Read
[the implementation status](https://github.com/susumutomita/TenkaCloud/blob/main/infrastructure/README.md)
before describing any cloud capability as working. The historical launcher's older
backend options are not additional current hosting modes. Do not print credentials
or ask users to paste them into chat. A successful build is not an event rehearsal:
check organizer/participant sign-in, team isolation, scoring, restart and cleanup.

## Read the code by the symptom

Paths below are relative to the platform checkout. Start with the affected row and
nearby tests, then trace callers and consumers. Do not scan the entire repository
before making a small change.

| Symptom or change | Entry point |
| --- | --- |
| Local startup or catalog availability | `scripts/local-host/main.ts`, `scripts/local-host/` |
| Event/team setup | `apps/application-admin-console/src/pages/EventDetail.tsx` |
| Participant answer or score display | `apps/participant-portal/src/`, then `scripts/local-host/service.ts` or `infrastructure/lib/problem-deploy/handlers/cloud-api/` |
| Deployment or backend configuration | `infrastructure/templates/cloud-pipeline.yaml`, `scripts/cloud-hosting/main.ts`, `infrastructure/lib/problem-deploy/control-data/` |
| Problem rules, hints, or game UI | `problems/<category>/<problem>/metadata.json`, its runtime/plugin, and `portal/` |
| Shared API or scoring contract | `packages/portal-contracts/`, `packages/problem-sdk/`, corresponding producers and consumers |

For a checkout, read `AGENTS.md`; `CLAUDE.md` is just an import of it. Preserve the
parent and submodule revisions and unrelated work. Trace input → handler/rule →
stored state → displayed result. Report the actual failing step and evidence.
Required commit verification is `make before-commit`; use focused tests while editing.
Apply existing authorization and ask before unapproved destructive actions, releases,
shared-environment changes, or secret access. Read-only investigation can proceed.

## Prompts a user can give their assistant

- 「TenkaCloud をローカルで試したい。この端末の前提条件を確認して、問題を1つ開始し、回答の結果が見えるところまで進めて。」
- 「TenkaCloud を AWS に構築したい。DB 費用を抑える Turso の手順を使い、既存環境の有無と必要な設定を調べて。構成・費用・撤去方法を提示してからデプロイする。」
- 「この不具合について、画面から API、保存、得点表示までの関係を該当ファイルで説明して。根拠を確認してから修正し、実行した検証と未確認事項を分けて報告して。」

## Book

- [Build Your Own Cloud Competition (English)](https://leanpub.com/build-your-own-cloud-competition)
- [『自分で作るクラウド競技』(日本語)](https://zenn.dev/bull/books/cloud-competition)

These explain design decisions, **not** a specification. Current code and tests take precedence.
